shipped.title_o: The next Big Five Inventory (BFI-2): Developing and assessing a hierarchical model with 15 facets to enhance bandwidth, fidelity, and predictive power.
shipped.outcome_quote: Results indicated that the structure found in the English version was replicated in the Dutch adaptation.

blind_target.authors: Soto, C. J., & John, O. P.
blind_target.title: The next big five inventory (BFI-2): Developing and assessing a hierarchical model with 15 facets to enhance bandwidth, fidelity, and predictive power.
blind_target.evidence_quote:
Soto and John (2017b) investigated the psychometric
properties of the English-language BFI–2, using U.S. samples. They found evidence for the reliability, structure, and
convergent and predictive validity of the instrument. First, we wanted to examine whether the good psychometric
properties of the original BFI–2 would replicate in samples
of Dutch adults.
blind_target.outcome_quote:
Overall, we replicated the support
that Soto and John (2017b) reported for the structural validity of the English BFI–2, as well as the convergent validity
and internal consistency of its domain and facet scales.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall replication verdict in the conclusion takes precedence over specific psychometric discrepancies.

items.parent_review_question: Resolve same-author/year papers, long versus short-form psychometric targets, and actual retests versus materials citations.

shipped.title_o: Motion as Motivation: Using Repetitive Flexion Movements to Stimulate the Approach System
shipped.outcome_quote: Taken together, the effects of repeated flexion movements were inconsistent and weak.

blind_target.title: Motion as Motivation: Using Repetitive Flexion Movements to Stimulate the Approach System.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Study 1 was a direct replication that used the same task, equipment, and experimental computer design as Haeffel ( 2011 ).
blind_target.outcome_quote: We conducted two studies to test the effect of repeated flexion finger movements on approach motivation. The results of the two studies were inconsistent with each other as well as with the original Haeffel ( 2011 ) study (see Figure 1 ).
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors judge the two studies inconsistent with the original and argue significant effects are likely chance. Neither replication recovers the original BAS-Fun and gender-dependent persistence findings; significant findings occur on different outcomes. Maxwell and Davidson supplied the adapted task rather than the finding directly retested.

items.parent_review_question: Assess whether the authors give an overall failure verdict despite inconsistent direct/conceptual patterns; distinguish central replicated findings from ancillary nulls.

shipped.title_o: ERN and the placebo: A misattribution approach to studying the arousal properties of the error-related negativity.
shipped.outcome_quote: ERN/Ne differences between misattribution and control group could not be replicated, although the statistical power of the replication study was high.

blind_target.title: ERN and the placebo: a misattribution approach to studying the arousal properties of the error-related negativity.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Therefore, the aim of the present study was to investigate whether an experimental manipulation of the misattribution of state-anxiety following errors modulates the ERN/Ne. To this end, we aimed at replicating the findings of Inzlicht and Al-Khindi (2012).
blind_target.outcome_quote: As Inzlicht and Al-Khindi (2012), we did not observe performance differences between both groups. However, ERN/Ne differences between misattribution and control group could not be replicated, although the statistical power of the replication study was high. Evidence regarding the replication of performance and the non-replication of ERN/Ne findings was confirmed by Bayesian statistics.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Explicit comparison confirms the original null performance finding but fails the ERN/Ne effect. The introduction expressly says replication of the null performance result is as important as replication of the ERN/Ne result; thus both are planned target findings. There is no overall verdict overriding these contrasting comparisons. The terminology reproducibility refers here to a new sample, not reanalysis of original data.

items.parent_review_question: Assess the explicit planned null performance replication against the ERN title-focus rule; decide whether performance is a central finding or an ancillary check.
